summary_zh: 9 个调研方向、239 个开源项目（去重后）。结论：44 个采用、55 个备选、84 个仅作参考、56 个避免。主引擎 Apache ECharts 6.1，地图 Leaflet 1.9.4（离线 Natural Earth 底图），交互表格 Tabulator 6.6，版式表格与动效为自研（零依赖）。完整报告见 research/landscape.md。

angles.summary:
I surveyed 30+ JS charting libraries. Versions, licences and dates come from the live npm registry on 2026-10-14; gzip sizes were measured on the real dist files. Every candidate's classic-script build was smoke-tested from file:// in headless Chromium 141.

**Primary engine: Apache ECharts 6.1.0** (Apache-2.0, ASF-governed, 67.5k stars). Use the full UMD dist/echarts.min.js (359 KB gz), which is already vendored. That choice is confirmed.
- It is the only permissive engine that covers nearly the whole IB chart vocabulary in one classic script. That includes calendar, parallel, geo, sankey, treemap, sunburst, boxplot, candlestick and gauge.
- ECharts 6 added chord, beeswarm/jitter, axis breaks, a matrix coordinate system, runtime setTheme() and reusable custom series. All were verified working under file://.
- It has both an SVG renderer and a canvas renderer. The SVG renderer printed to PDF as vector with selectable text. Canvas printed as a ~104 ppi raster, but handled 200k points with LTTB in about 290 ms.
- Node SSR (renderToSVGString) runs from the same UMD file.

**Pitchbook recipes in ECharts:** a 6-chart pitchbook page all rendered cleanly:
- EBITDA bridge with connectors and a v6 axis break
- Marimekko and football field
- 4-dimension bubble via visualMap
- CAGR bracket

Waterfall, Mekko and football field are custom-series recipes of 20–40 lines, not native series.

**Complements:**
- @echarts-x/custom-* series (violin, bar-range, line-range, contour), adopt as needed.
- uPlot 1.6.32 (21 KB gz) for table sparklines and >1M-point series.
- D3 7.9 as a utility layer (d3-format, scale, hierarchy, geo).
- A lazy-loaded Vega-Lite 6.5 / Vega 6.4 / vega-embed 7.3 stack (~275 KB gz) for an optional explore/ask console. It has the best declarative cross-filtering, is the most LLM-friendly grammar, and interoperates with Altair. Keep it out of printed pages.
- echarts-gl only if 3D vol surfaces are needed.
- Plotly.js 4.1.2 only for plotly.py parity or scientific charts. It is heavy: 1.44 MB gz full, 422 KB finance bundle.

**Avoid:**
- ApexCharts went proprietary in 5.1.0 and is free only under US$2M revenue; the last MIT release is 5.0.0.
- AG Charts Community lacks waterfall, sankey, heatmap, box, candlestick, radar, funnel, treemap, zoom, navigator and animation; I confirmed these trigger Enterprise warnings.
- Highcharts, amCharts 5 (logo linkware) and ZingChart (watermark) are commercial; use them as reference only.
- Lightweight Charts carries a mandatory TradingView attribution notice and link.
- React-only libraries (Recharts, Nivo, visx) are out, since React 19 dropped UMD builds.
- Stale or broken: Taucharts, Frappe, C3, Britecharts, Toast UI, Vizzu (ESM+WASM fails on file://) and Unovis (no UMD).

AntV G2 5.4 and VisActor VChart 2.1 are strong MIT alternatives with native Mekko/mosaic, waterfall and storytelling motion. They are canvas-first, Chinese-first in docs, corporate-governed and heavier (VChart 617 KB gz). Borrow ideas from them; don't switch.
insights:
Keep ECharts 6.1.0 as the primary engine; the vendored full UMD (359 KB gz) is confirmed. Every v6 headline feature works from file:// in Chromium 141:
- chord
- beeswarm (xAxis.jitter + jitterOverlap:false)
- axis breaks (yAxis.breaks, plus expand/collapse/toggleAxisBreak actions)
- matrix coordinate system
- runtime chart.setTheme()
- registerCustomSeries

Default to the SVG renderer.
- In a Chromium PDF, SVG charts stayed vector with selectable text (pdftotext extracted the labels).
- A canvas chart was embedded as a 600x340 raster at ~104 ppi.
- Use canvas only above ~5k marks, with devicePixelRatio of at least 2 and a print snapshot on beforeprint.

think-cell-style exhibits are ECharts custom-series recipes of 20–40 lines each, all verified rendering cleanly:
- waterfall with dashed connectors and (negative) labels
- Marimekko on value x value axes
- football field (transparent stack + markLine)
- CAGR bracket via graphic + convertToPixel (recompute on resize)

The v6 axis break gives think-cell's broken value axis through bridge totals. Register these as named custom series (RK.series.*).
Custom series are not clipped by default; set clip:true. Combining yAxis.min with tall total bars otherwise overflows the grid; an axis break is the correct pitchbook fix.

Keep chart chrome in HTML: title, units, source and footnotes. In the test, an in-canvas title, legend and yAxis.name overlapped. HTML chrome also gives consistent typography, Ctrl+F, accessibility and cleaner PPT export.

ECharts 6 default-behaviour changes to guard against with a pinned theme and screenshot diffs:
- 6.0: new default theme with the legend at the bottom; anti-overflow axis layout (grid.outerBoundsMode); rich labels inherit plain label styles (richInheritPlainLabel); geo/graph center percent base changed.
- 6.1: containShape keeps edge bars inside the grid; tooltip.valueFormatter's 2nd argument is now rawDataIndex; axis.startValue is decoupled from min; an XSS in the lines tooltip was fixed.

ECharts Node SSR works from the same UMD file: init(null, null, {renderer:'svg', ssr:true}) then renderToSVGString(), about 60 ms per chart in Node 22. The Python builder can pre-render static SVG fallbacks for print, PPT, e-mail and thumbnails. echarts/ssr/client can hydrate them.

Locale gotcha: under LANG=C, headless Chromium reports navigator.language='en-US@posix', and uPlot, Carbon and Lightweight Charts then crash with 'Invalid language tag'. The Playwright PDF/PNG step must set locale:'en-US', and kit formatters must strip '@…' before calling Intl.NumberFormat.

Licence drift is real: ApexCharts moved from MIT (5.0.0, 2025-07-09) to a proprietary dual licence in 5.1.0, free only under US$2M revenue. Pin exact versions in vendor.json and re-run `npm view pkg@ver license` in CI before any bump.

AG Charts Community is a demo tier for IB use. Waterfall, sankey, heatmap, box-plot, candlestick, radar, funnel, treemap, zoom, navigator and animation all emit 'enterprise features' warnings and do not render.

Attribution and branding traps:
- Lightweight Charts (Apache-2.0 plus a mandatory TradingView notice and link)
- amCharts 5 (logo must stay unless paid)
- ZingChart (watermark)
- Highcharts (credits link; client-facing use needs a SaaS licence)

'ESM-only' does not mean no UMD: Vega 6 declares ESM-only, yet build/vega.min.js, vega-lite.min.js and vega-embed.min.js still ship and work on file://. Always check the jsdelivr dist listing. True ESM+WASM libraries (Vizzu, Perspective, DuckDB-WASM) fail on file:// because of CORS.

Vega-Lite is the right lazy-loaded complement for a future 'ask your data' console: declarative cross-filter params, bind:'scales' zoom, an expression-language calculate transform, JSON-schema validation of LLM output, and Altair interop. It has no animation and no sankey, chord or radar, so keep it out of printed pitchbook pages.

Python should emit kit component config plus a dataset, not raw ECharts options, because formatter functions cannot be JSON. JS components compile config into an option. Excel-like format codes (#,##0.0;(#,##0.0), 0.0x, 0.0%) should compile to JS formatters, since ECharts has no format-string system. pyecharts 2.1.0 already targets ECharts 6 assets.

For multi-dimensional encoding, ECharts visualMap is the workhorse: colour, colorAlpha, lightness, symbolSize, symbol and opacity per dimension, with several maps (6.1 seriesTargets). inRange/outOfRange styling doubles as instant cross-filter feedback. The tested bubble chart encoded x, y, size, colour (sector) and alpha (ROIC).

Cross-filter pattern: own the state store outside the engine.
1. ECharts brushSelected, legendselectchanged, datazoom or click events feed the store.
2. Each component calls setOption({dataset}, {replaceMerge:['dataset']}).
3. ECharts diff-animates the change.

Use universalTransition plus dataGroupId for drill and morph effects, echarts.connect for synced tooltips and zoom, and dispose() on re-mount.

Plotly 4 gotchas:
- Geo traces fetch topojson from cdn.plot.ly; preload via window.PlotlyGeoAssets.
- The new culori colour parser renders rgb() fractions near-black.
- mapbox traces were removed.
- The full bundle is 1.44 MB gz.
Category axes sort alphabetically by default in Vega-Lite and Observable Plot (the smoke test showed COGS, D&A, EBIT, Opex, Rev). Always pass an explicit order.
React-based libraries (Recharts, Nivo, visx, Victory, MUI X) are out: React 19 removed its UMD builds, and most of these have no classic-script dist.

angles.summary: Keep Leaflet 1.9.4 (BSD-2, 42 KB gz, classic UMD) as the primary map engine and add ECharts 6.1 geo as the second. Both are already vendored. Leaflet 2.0 is still only 2.0.0-alpha.1 (Aug 2025), with no beta or rc. It drops factory methods, and in my test the 1.x plugins broke: the V1 polyfill rescued leaflet.heat and markercluster, but not leaflet-ant-path. I ran 17 offline tests (pages opened via file:// in headless Chromium, outbound requests blocked). They passed for Leaflet with its plugins, ECharts, deck.gl 9.4 UMD, OpenLayers 10.11, Observable Plot, MapLibre 5.24 UMD and AntV L7. L7 is the exception on network calls: it fetches its logo from gw.alipayobjects.com unless logoVisible:false. MapLibre 6 (July 2026) is ESM-only and WebGL2-only, and Chrome blocks it under file:// with a CORS error. 5.24.0 is the last UMD build and is now frozen. It still works offline with inline GeoJSON and with in-memory PMTiles via addProtocol, and draws labels with local fonts when glyph files can't load. Critical bug: world-atlas TopoJSON is spherical and stitched across the date line, so every planar renderer draws horizontal streaks from Russia, Fiji and Antarctica. Only d3 and Observable Plot draw it cleanly. Fix: cut the polygons at ±180°. In JS this is d3.geoProject with an identity equirectangular projection (verified: 7 to 0 jumps in 25 ms), but it is better done once in the Python builder. world-atlas is also archived, still on Natural Earth 4.1.0, and its 110m file has no Singapore, Hong Kong, Macao, Bahrain, Malta, Cayman or Bermuda. Rebuild the basemap from Natural Earth 5.1.2 10m simplified 1% with keep-shapes: about 109 KB, keeps these micro-states, and allows China point-of-view boundaries. Join on ISO_A3_EH or ADM0_A3, because ISO_A3 is -99 for France and Norway. Verified ECharts features worth reusing: pies placed on geo coordinates (replaces the GPL leaflet.minichart), heatmap on geo, brush selection on geo for cross-filtering, d3 projections (Equal Earth, China Albers, Pacific-centred) and the map↔bar morph. China maps need a 审图号 (map review number) for PRC audiences. The DataV/AMap GeoJSON used in most ECharts tutorials is licensed for learning only, and GADM is non-commercial. So: Natural Earth admin-1 (public domain) for global audiences; a licensed, reviewed base map or a tile-grid cartogram for PRC audiences. deck.gl 9.4 (575 KB gz) should be an optional lazy engine for 10k+ points or flows. kepler.gl, L7, Mapbox, Leaflet.VectorGrid (Beerware) and leaflet.minichart (GPL) are reference-only or avoid.
insights: ANTIMERIDIAN BUG (verified in 6 engines): world-atlas TopoJSON is stitched for spherical d3 rendering. Leaflet, MapLibre, deck.gl, OpenLayers, L7 and ECharts' default projection all draw horizontal streaks from Russia/Chukotka, Fiji and Antarctica. Fix: d3.geoProject(fc, d3.geoEquirectangular().scale(180/Math.PI).translate([0,0]).reflectY(true).precision(0)) removes all 7 jumps in 25 ms; better, cut once in the Python builder (antimeridian, Apache-2.0, or shapely).

WINDING RULE: d3, Plot and ECharts-with-d3-projection need raw spherical geometry. Feeding the planar-cut, reflected geometry into a d3 projection inverted 2 polygons and filled the whole globe. Keep raw and cut variants, and assert d3.geoArea(f) < 2π in tests.

world-atlas 2.0.2 is archived and on Natural Earth 4.1.0. Its 110m file has no Singapore, Hong Kong, Macao, Bahrain, Malta, Cayman or Bermuda, the key financial centres for a bank. Natural Earth 5.1.2 10m simplified 1% keep-shapes is about the same size (109 KB raw / 36 KB gz) and keeps them.

Natural Earth ISO gotcha: ISO_A3/ISO_N3 are -99 for France and Norway (plus N. Cyprus, Somaliland, Kosovo); join on ISO_A3_EH or ADM0_A3. NE admin-0 also carries NAME_ZH/NAME_ZHT and 33 FCLASS_* worldview columns.

Natural Earth 5.x point-of-view variants (31 worldviews incl. China): ne_10m_admin_0_countries_chn merges Taiwan into China, keeps HK/Macao separate with SOVEREIGNT=China, and has a 9-dash-line indicator layer. Defaults are de facto boundaries.

Leaflet without tile layers: map.getMaxZoom() is Infinity. markercluster throws 'Map has no maxZoom specified', and leaflet.heat divides intensity by 2^12 (faint heat). Always set minZoom/maxZoom (kit geo-heat already resets heat maxZoom to the fitted zoom).

Leaflet 2.0 is still alpha.1 (Aug 2025), with no beta/rc 14+ months after the first alpha. leaflet-global.js still sets window.L, but factories are removed, so 1.x plugins break. The V1 polyfill fixed heat and markercluster but not ant-path ('Class constructor cannot be invoked without new'). Stay on 1.9.4 and write constructor-style, 2.0-ready code.

MapLibre GL JS 6.0 (2026-07-22) is ESM-only and WebGL2-only, with a module worker, and is blocked by CORS on file://. 5.24.0 is the last UMD and works offline: inline style + GeoJSON, in-memory PMTiles via addProtocol, and labels drawn with local fonts when glyph PBF fetches fail.

file:// rules: fetch/XHR, ES modules and module workers are blocked; blob workers and tiles from relative folders work (local raster tiles verified). Geo data must ship as classic JS (RK.geo.register). PMTiles works only through a custom in-memory Source over a base64-embedded buffer, verified in both protomaps-leaflet and MapLibre 5.

Offline network audit with requests blocked: Leaflet, ECharts, deck.gl, OpenLayers, Plot, MapLibre 5 and PMTiles made 0 external requests. AntV L7 made 1 (logo from gw.alipayobjects.com), fixed with logoVisible:false. This matters for confidentiality and for clients behind proxies.

ECharts 6.1 geo features verified offline: pie series with coordinateSystem:'geo' (replaces GPL leaflet.minichart), heatmap on geo, brush (rect/polygon) on geo with brushSelected data indices for cross-filtering, SVG renderer (heatmap becomes one raster <image>), projection.stream with d3 Equal Earth/conic/rotate for Pacific-centred or equal-area maps, registerMap specialAreas for insets, and the official 'Morphing between Map and Bar' example.

Licence red flags: leaflet.minichart GPL-2.0+; world-geojson GPL-3.0; Leaflet.VectorGrid Beerware; leaflet.pattern has no licence; Mapbox GL JS v2+ proprietary; DataV.GeoAtlas data is 'learning use only' (from 高德); GADM bans commercial use and redistribution; geoBoundaries is CC BY 4.0; Protomaps/OSM tiles are ODbL (attribution; review distribution of extracts).

Tile policies: the OSM tile server forbids offline use and bulk prefetch and may withdraw commercial access at any time; CARTO basemaps need an Enterprise licence for commercial use (free key = 5M tiles/month, non-commercial intent). Never default to online tiles; vector Natural Earth basemaps in theme colours look more 'pitchbook' anyway.

China compliance: publicly shown China maps need a 审图号. The 自然资源部 标准地图 can be used unmodified with its number, but cropping or zooming requires review. Microsoft suspended Excel map charts for China users. For PRC audiences, use a licensed or reviewed base, or a tile-grid cartogram (with Taiwan/HK/Macao tiles); Natural Earth admin-1 (32 CHN features with name_zh, iso_3166_2) suits global audiences only.

China province projection: d3.geoConicEqualArea().parallels([25,47]).rotate([-105,0]) through ECharts projection hooks, or Proj4Leaflet '+proj=aea +lat_1=25 +lat_2=47 +lon_0=105'. Join on GB/T 2260 adcodes (province-city-china, MIT) or ISO 3166-2:CN letter codes (CN-BJ).

Flow maps: avoid great-circle plugins (Leaflet.Arc wraps at the date line). Use quadratic Bézier SVG arcs with width ∝ value, arrowheads (direction survives print), node circles sized by in+out flow, and top-N aggregation above ~60 flows. For Americas–Asia flows a Pacific-centred view (ECharts + d3 rotate([-150,0])) reads better.

Bubbles: use L.circleMarker (pixel radius) not L.circle (metres); sqrt area scale; draw largest first; nested-circle legend; Leaflet draws circleMarkers as <path>, so animate radius with rAF tweens, not CSS r transitions.

Density: prefer hexbin (quantitative legend, crisp print) over blur heatmaps in pitchbooks; leaflet.heat and ECharts heatmaps are relative and raster. Use deck.gl HexagonLayer/HeatmapLayer (GPU) for 100k+ points.

Print: SVG engines (Leaflet SVG, ECharts SVG, Plot) print as vectors; WebGL/canvas engines (deck, MapLibre, L7, OL, Leaflet canvas, heatmaps) print as rasters. Hide zoom controls in print and call invalidateSize on beforeprint.

Leaflet in long reports: disable scrollWheelZoom or use gesture handling (leaflet-gesture-handling, MIT); call map.invalidateSize() from a ResizeObserver for maps in hidden tabs or collapsed sections.

angles.summary: Pitchbook tables should be hand-built: a small in-house RK.Table and RK.Sensitivity component (DOM <table>, CSS tokens, inline-SVG micro-charts). Comps, precedents, financial summaries and sensitivity tables are static, dense, under 500 cells and typeset to bank conventions: phantom-parenthesis decimal alignment, NM/NA rules, x and % suffixes, underlined group headers, a target row excluded from Mean/Median/High/Low rows, footnotes. Every grid library fights these details, while a DOM table prints as vectors, repeats headers on each page, pastes into Excel/PowerPoint and works with Ctrl+F at zero dependency cost. For large, interactive or editable lists, adopt Tabulator 6.6.1 (MIT, UMD tabulator.min.js, ~103 KB gz, DOM). It covers frozen columns, nested headers, groupBy with group calcs, range selection and fill handle, printAsHtml and CSV/XLSX/PDF download. Gotchas: only one top and one bottom calc per column, built-in calcs return strings, and XLSX output is unstyled. AG Grid Community 36.2.0 (MIT, ~522 KB gz) is the runner-up; it has multi-row pinnedBottomRowData for stats rows, column groups and pinning, but grouping, aggregation, pivot, Excel export, sparklines, clipboard, range selection and formulas are Enterprise ($999/dev). For an optional, lazy-loaded pivot or cross-tab data explorer, adopt AntV S2 2.7.2 (MIT, UMD ~310 KB gz, canvas). It has totals and subtotals, tree mode, conditions (background, interval bars, icons), built-in line/bar/bullet mini charts and copy/export, but defaults to Chinese labels unless S2.setLang('en_US') is called. VisActor VTable 1.26.8 is the heavier alternative (~544 KB gz plus ~358 KB gz of plugins); it adds sparkline and progress-bar cells, pivot charts and a built-in appear animation. Never use canvas grids for the primary printed tables. Headless Chromium tests confirmed that Tabulator, AG Grid, S2, VTable, DataTables 3 (now jQuery-free), Grid.js, Cheetah Grid, SlickGrid (needs SortableJS) and write-excel-file all work from file://. Perspective (now @perspective-dev 5.6.0, Apache-2.0; ESM + WASM loaded via import.meta.url) fails with a CORS error, so keep it for a Step-2 served mode, where its ExprTK expression columns fit client-typed formulas. For styled XLSX export use write-excel-file 4.1.1 (MIT, ~19 KB gz: number formats, fills, borders, merges, frozen panes, formulas). For reading client files use SheetJS CE 0.20.3 from cdn.sheetjs.com only, because npm xlsx@0.18.5 has CVE-2023-30533 and CVE-2024-22363. Use browser print CSS for PDF. Avoid Grid.js (stale), Glide (React-only, stale), RevoGrid (Stencil ESM; export and pivot are Pro), PivotTable.js (jQuery, 2018), simple-datatables (LGPL), HyperFormula (GPL) and WebDataRocks (EULA, ~1 MB cap). Handsontable, Flexmonster and AG Grid Enterprise are reference only. Define tables with a declarative JSON TableSpec (columns, formats, NM rules, stats, heat, sparkline cells, expression columns). It renders through RK.Table and can be adapted to Tabulator, AG Grid or S2, and it gives the future local LLM a safe, code-free target.
insights: Split tables into three layers. (1) Hand-built RK.Table for printed pitchbook tables (comps, precedents, sensitivities). (2) Tabulator for large or editable interactive lists. (3) Lazy-loaded S2 (or VTable) for pivot exploration. Canvas grids never carry primary printed tables.

Verified under file:// in headless Chromium 141: Tabulator, AG Grid CE, S2, VTable, DataTables 3, Grid.js, Cheetah Grid, SlickGrid (with SortableJS) and write-excel-file all work as classic scripts. Perspective 5.6.0 fails because it is ESM with top-level await and fetches WASM via import.meta.url.

On file://, fetch() of local files fails, but window.isSecureContext is true, navigator.clipboard exists and Blob plus <a download> works. Ship data as data/*.js (window.__RK_DATA__) or inline <script type=application/json>. Copy and download buttons work offline.

Tabulator gotchas: only one topCalc and one bottomCalc per column, so Mean, Median, High and Low need tfoot, a separate stats table or pinned synthetic rows. Built-in calcs return precision-formatted strings. XLSX download is unstyled (SheetJS CE). Printing needs printAsHtml or only the virtual viewport prints.

AG Grid Community does include multi-row pinnedBottomRowData (ideal for stats rows), column groups, pinning, CSV and print layout. Grouping, aggregation, pivot, Excel export, sparklines, clipboard, range selection, formulas and calculated columns are Enterprise ($999/dev). Vendor only ag-grid-community to avoid a watermark or licence breach.

AntV S2 defaults to Chinese labels ('总计' for grand total), so call S2.setLang('en_US'). Its conditions API (text, background, interval, icon with a regex field) and built-in line/bar/bullet mini charts map well to bank heat tables.

VTable: container size must be integer pixels; aggregation rows need bottomFrozenRowCount; @visactor/vtable-export is deprecated in favour of vtable-plugins TableExportPlugin (ExcelJS-based, +358 KB gz). animationAppear (one-by-one by row or column) is a good model for tasteful table entry motion.

Perspective moved npm scope from @finos (frozen at 3.8.0) to @perspective-dev (5.6.0, repo perspective-dev/perspective). Its ExprTK expression columns and DuckDB virtual servers suit the future client-formula, served-mode step.
DataTables 3.0 (2026-07-22) dropped jQuery; the UMD dataTables.min.js sets window.DataTable. It is a viable progressive enhancer for Python-rendered static tables.
Never npm install xlsx: 0.18.5 is the last npm version and carries CVE-2023-30533 and CVE-2024-22363. Get SheetJS CE 0.20.3 from cdn.sheetjs.com. CE writes no fills or fonts.

write-excel-file 4.1.1 (MIT, ~19 KB gz, UMD global writeXlsxFile) exports styled XLSX: Excel number formats such as 0.0"x" and #,##0.0_);(#,##0.0), fills, per-side borders, spans, formulas and frozen panes. The v4 API is writeXlsxFile(...).toBlob()/.toFile().

Pitchbook typesetting conventions: right-aligned tabular figures; a phantom ')' on positives so decimals align with '(3.4)'; x and % suffixes; NM for negative or >100x multiples; NA; en dash for zero; target row tinted and excluded from stats; bold stats rows after a rule; gapped underlines under group headers; no vertical gridlines; unit line, as-of date, superscript footnotes and source line.

CSS gotchas: border-collapse:collapse plus position:sticky loses header borders, so use separate with border-spacing:0. Heat fills need print-color-adjust:exact to print. Use thead{display:table-header-group} and tr{break-inside:avoid} for paginated print, and unset sticky in print. CSS text-align:'.' is unsupported.

Heat colouring: compute the domain from non-target, non-NM values, clip at percentiles, diverge around the median for multiples (reversed for growth and margins), interpolate in OKLab/OKLCH with muted lightness, flip text to white on dark fills, always show a legend and make heat opt-in per column. Bake fills into XLSX on export.

In-cell micro-charts should be inline SVG (sparkline with last, min and max dots; two-sided data bars from a zero axis; bullet; 52-week range dot; win/loss), not one ECharts instance per cell. SVG stays vector in print and themes via currentColor.

Sensitivity tables (WACC x terminal growth, entry x exit multiple to IRR) are trivial in HTML: boxed base case, optional diverging fill vs current price. Optionally make them live via an rk.expr formula plus axis steppers to show dynamic re-rendering.

Table motion should be restrained: FLIP row reorder on sort and filter (~240ms), cross-fade recomputed stats, data bars growing on first reveal with stagger capped near 400ms, colour transitions on heat changes. No count-up on dense numeric tables. Honour prefers-reduced-motion and disable all motion in print.

Define tables via a declarative JSON TableSpec (columns and groups, fmt, NM rules, expr calculated columns, stats rows with exclude rule, heat, cell types, footnotes, export, interactions). It renders through RK.Table, can be adapted to Tabulator, AG Grid or S2, and gives a local LLM a safe target to edit (Step 2).

Licence traps to block in vendor.json review: HyperFormula (GPL-3.0), simple-datatables (LGPL-3.0), WebDataRocks (proprietary EULA, ~1 MB data cap), Handsontable (proprietary; only one 90-day evaluation for businesses), RevoGrid Pro, AG Grid Enterprise, Flexmonster. JSZip is dual MIT/GPL, so elect MIT.

angles.summary: I took the conventions from primary sources: recent bank 'Discussion Materials' that Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, Evercore, Rothschild & Co and Centerview filed on SEC EDGAR as EX-99.(c) exhibits (2023-2026). I looked at the page images and sampled their colours. Pitchbook pages are US Letter landscape (11x8.5in, ratio 1.294) and Rothschild uses 4:3; none of the samples is 16:9. The report-kit page container should therefore default to 1056x816 CSS px, with A4 and 16:9 as options. Every page has the same parts: a section tracker, a one-sentence action title, a units line ('($ in millions, except per share data)'), navy chart banners, the chart or table with a commentary or key-figures side panel, numbered footnotes, a mandatory 'Source:' line with the as-of date, a draft or confidential stamp, and a page number. Colour use is restrained: a navy primary, steel-blue for the comparison series, greys, one accent, and a red or claret dashed line for the offer price. The subject company versus its peers is shown by emphasis, not by giving each company its own colour. I built 3 themes (navy, bronze, slate). Each has structural tokens plus an 8-colour categorical palette in light and dark versions, and all 6 palettes pass every hard check of the dataviz validator (contrast, colour-blind separation, lightness and chroma). Each theme also has a validated single-hue ramp, a sequential ramp and a diverging ramp. Number formatting differs by 'house style' (GS writes '$ 44.71' and '7.6 x'; others write '$2.27' and '7.9x'), so the format layer needs configurable presets. Fixed rules across houses: negatives in parentheses; n.m. kept out of mean/median; n.a. and the dash kept distinct; units only on the first and total rows; and think-cell-style rounding so displayed parts add up to the displayed total. The wish-list has 34 components with data fields and encodings. The 12 must-have components are: football field, share price + volume + events, indexed performance, comps table, precedents table, sensitivity grid, waterfall, analysis at various prices, premiums paid, multiple history with '% of time in range', financial summary, and think-cell-style columns (CAGR arrows, difference arrows, value lines, totals). Engine: keep ECharts 6.1 (already vendored, Apache-2.0). Version 6 adds axis breaks, a matrix layout, chord diagrams, beeswarm/jitter and runtime theme switching including dark mode. Add the official @echarts-x/custom-bar-range (1.8KB auto-registering classic script) for range bars and simple-statistics for regression and quantiles. Use HTML tables for comps, sensitivity and AVP so they can be copied into Excel, and Tabulator only if heavy grid interaction is needed. License and offline hazards: ApexCharts 8 is now free only below $2M revenue, MapLibre GL 6 ships only ES modules (fails under file://), lightweight-charts requires TradingView attribution, GSAP's license is not OSI-approved, and Plotly is 1.44MB gzipped and pulls map data from a CDN by default.
insights: Page size: US bank pitchbooks are US Letter landscape (11x8.5in, aspect 1.294), verified on GS, Morgan Stanley and Evercore EDGAR page images. Rothschild uses 4:3 and none of the samples is 16:9. Default the page container to 1056x816 CSS px with @page size 11in 8.5in, and offer A4 landscape (EMEA/Asia) and 16:9.

Page anatomy is consistent across all banks: section tracker (caps label, navy tab, or footer section name), action title, units line '($ in millions, except per share data)', navy banner chart headers, a side panel (commentary bullets with bold lead-ins, or a 'Select data points' KPI table), superscript-numbered footnotes, a mandatory 'Source:' line with the as-of date, a draft/confidential stamp, and a page number. Footnote numbering should be automated per page.

Colour is semantic emphasis, not categorical. Subject company = dark navy, peers = steel-blue or grey, mean/median = dashed lines, offer/current price = red or claret dashed reference line with an italic label, 'For reference only' methods = light/grey bars. Typically 4-5 colours per page.

Validated palettes (all PASS in both light and dark mode). navy light: #2e64a6,#b68028,#9f3960,#4b99c9,#57873a,#7555a8,#cb5f31,#008e88; navy dark (#0f1724): #4c82c6,#bd8630,#b74e74,#449fc9,#639346,#8a69be,#d5683b,#129d97. bronze light (#fbf9f5): #aa6926,#37649e,#8f2c47,#a68922,#008b9d,#cb6443,#865695,#469364. slate light: #3e6dc8,#db6143,#009783,#7d5abc,#3e9245,#379fc7,#c38700,#c35f92. The first 3 colours of each also pass all-pairs checks for scatter, bubble and map charts.

Navy structural tokens: ink #0b2545 (15.4:1), banner #12355f (white text 12.4:1), navy-700 #1f4e79, steel #6f97c7, tint #e6edf6, stat-row #f2f4f7, muted #6b7280, gold accent #b68028, reference red #b3261e. Single-hue navy ramp #0e2a47,#1f4e79,#3a6fa6,#6b93c4,#98b4d8 passes the ordinal checks; use it for stacked segments to get the classic monochrome IB look.

Number formatting varies by house style (GS: '$ 44.71', '7.6 x', '(0.9)%', '05-Dec-2025'; others: '$2.27', '7.9x', '(32%)', 'Apr '24'; units mm/MM/m, bn/Bn). Make these configurable house-style settings in rk.format (currencySpace, multSpace, percent parentheses inside or outside, unit suffix, date styles) rather than hard-coding them.

Table rule from the GS DCF/AVP/precedents pages: only the first row and subtotal/total rows carry $, x or %; middle rows are bare numbers. Subtotals bold with a top rule, a dashed vertical line between stub/historical and projected columns, the terminal column shaded, the subject company row highlighted, and stats rows (Max/75th/Mean/Median/25th/Min) on a grey background separated from the data rows.

n.m. (not meaningful: negative denominator or multiple above a house threshold), n.a. (missing) and the dash (zero or not applicable) must stay distinct. n.m. values are excluded from mean/median, and the threshold goes in a footnote.

The core of think-cell is its decoration layer and rounding, not its chart types: CAGR arrows, difference arrows, value lines, totals, axis breaks, 'Other' grouping, automatic black/white label contrast, and TCROUND-style sum-consistent rounding. Build these as reusable decoration plugins plus a roundToTotal (largest-remainder) utility.

Event annotation on price charts comes in 3 bank styles, and the kit should support all 3: boxed callouts with leader lines colour-coded by event category (GS), lettered badges on the line plus an event table (MS), and vertical drop lines with a bold date and text (Rothschild). Also: an end-of-line last-value label, a 52-week high/low and VWAP mini-table, and an undisturbed-date marker.

IB convention often uses a dual y-axis (price + volume, or price + EV/NTM EBITDA), which data-viz best practice forbids. Default to vertically stacked panes sharing the x-axis (ECharts multi-grid plus a linked dataZoom), and keep a dualAxis option for house-style compatibility with both axes titled and unitised.

Sensitivity, accretion/dilution, analysis-at-various-prices, comps and precedents should be HTML tables (copyable as TSV to Excel, accessible, sharp in print) with a highlighted base-case cell and low-saturation sequential or diverging backgrounds. Recompute live from formulas (rk.expr) when the client changes the axis centre or step, or types a new metric column.

Football field implementation: a method column (navy tabs with white text, grouped primary vs reference), range bars with outside-end value labels, dashed reference lines (offer, unaffected VWAP, current), and optional right-hand columns for implied TEV, multiple and premium (Evercore style). @echarts-x/custom-bar-range (Apache-2.0, 1.8KB auto-registering classic script) renders the bars; the text columns are HTML grid.

ECharts 6 capabilities confirmed by grepping the vendored build: axis breaks, matrix coordinate system, chord, beeswarm/jitter, setTheme for runtime and dark-mode switching, universalTransition, relativeTo label anchoring. There is no native waterfall series, so use a stacked bar with a transparent base or a custom series. Use the SVG renderer for print/PDF.

2026 license and offline traps: ApexCharts 8.x is dual-licensed and free only below $2M revenue (avoid). MapLibre GL 6.x is ESM-only .mjs and breaks under file:// (the last UMD build is 5.24.0). lightweight-charts requires NOTICE text and a tradingview.com link. GSAP 3.15 uses a non-OSI 'Standard no charge' license. Plotly is 1.44MB gzipped and fetches topojson from a CDN by default. Observable Plot's UMD build needs global d3, and Vega-Lite's needs global vega.

Fonts: bulge brackets use all-sans Arial-like type (bold navy or black titles); boutiques use a large serif title with sans body. Open replacements: Arimo/Tinos (Arial/Times metric-compatible, OFL, about 11.4KB per latin weight), Source Serif 4, Inter, IBM Plex. Noto Sans SC is about 3.4MB per weight, so it must be subset by the Python builder. Under file://, Firefox only loads fonts from the same directory or a subdirectory, so put them in ./fonts/ or base64-inline them.

Map the FT Visual Vocabulary families (deviation, correlation, ranking, distribution, change over time, magnitude, part-to-whole, spatial, flow) to IB components for gallery navigation. IB-specific forms with no FT equivalent: football field (range/dumbbell), sensitivity grid (XY heatmap as a table), AVP table, league table, tombstones, Harvey-ball matrix.

Anthropic's financial-services repo (Apache-2.0) codifies Excel-model conventions usable as defaults: section header fill #1F4E79, column header #D9E1F2, stats rows #F2F2F2, key output/base case #BDD7EE bold, blue input / black formula / green link font colours, 1-decimal multiples and percents, parentheses for negatives, and 'only blues and greys, 3-4 colours total'.

Strong interaction patterns for client use: time-range presets (1M/3M/6M/1Y/3Y/5Y/Since unaffected) with linked zoom across price, indexed and multiple charts; brushing the regression scatter filters the comps table; an offer-price slider updates the football field reference line and AVP premiums live; a peer-sample filter recomputes the premiums-paid percentiles; a re-base-to-100 date picker on the indexed chart.

Motion for a pitchbook feel: line clip reveal over 600-900ms with cubicOut, bars growing from the baseline over 400-600ms with a 30ms stagger, universalTransition morphing on data updates, KPI count-up; disabled for prefers-reduced-motion and print.

angles.summary:
The kit's core does not need a third-party animation library. Top data-journalism teams confirm this: the Pudding's svelte-starter has no animation dependency, and its Scrolly helper is about 80 lines of raw IntersectionObserver. Reuters' graphics-components uses only svelte-intersection-observer plus dotLottie. Chart motion should come from the already-vendored ECharts 6.1.0 (animationDurationUpdate, universalTransition, emphasis focus/blur). DOM motion should come from CSS transitions, WAAPI, IntersectionObserver and the View Transitions API, which became Baseline in October 2025 and was verified working under file:// in Chromium 141. The existing kit/core/rk.motion.js is the right base. It needs five additions: a beforeprint hook that mounts every lazily-mounted chart with animation off (otherwise charts outside the viewport print blank); a live listener for prefers-reduced-motion changes; an RK.motion.swap() wrapper around View Transitions; screen-reader-safe count-up; and skipping animation in hidden tabs.

GSAP 3.15.0 is free for commercial use under Webflow's 2025 Standard 'No Charge' License. That license is not OSI-approved, Webflow can amend or terminate it, and it bans use in no-code visual animation builders, so it should be avoided as a dependency. If a JS animation engine is ever needed, use MIT Motion 14.2.0: a motion/mini + inView + stagger IIFE built with esbuild is only 4.4 KB gz, versus 51 KB for the full UMD. anime.js 4.5.0 (MIT, 40.6 KB gz UMD) is the alternative for rich timelines.

For UI controls, adopt Tom Select 2.6.2 (Apache-2.0, 17.6 KB gz), noUiSlider 15.8.1 (MIT, 9.4 KB) and Floating UI 1.8.0 (MIT, 8.4 KB for core plus dom), with CSS anchor positioning (Baseline since January 2026) as a progressive enhancement. For dates, use native inputs with period presets, and Air Datepicker 3.6.0 only when a calendar is truly needed. Several candidates are now unmaintained or archived and should be avoided: flatpickr (last release 2022), Tippy (archived 2024-11), Shoelace (archived), Pico (archived 2026-10-04), AOS (last release 2018) and typed.js (now GPL-3.0). Web Awesome only ships ES modules, which fail to load under file://.

For icons, use Lucide 1.57.0 (ISC) as the primary set and Tabler Icons 3.49.0 (MIT, 366 finance/chart glyphs) as a secondary set. The Python builder must inline only the icons a report uses as a <symbol> sprite, because Chromium blocks external sprite references under file://.

For fonts: Fontsource's Inter keeps tnum (so the kit's tabular-nums CSS works) but drops zero, case and the ss/cv stylistic sets. Upstream inter-ui 4.1.1 provides a ~100 KB variable latin subset with every feature. Pair it with Source Serif 4 for headings and Noto Sans SC for Chinese. Noto Sans SC has no Reserved Font Name, so the builder can subset it to the report's text; Plex and Source fonts do reserve their names, so they should not be self-subset under the original name.
insights: file:// empirical test (Playwright Chromium 141): all 20 UMD/IIFE builds load and initialize as classic scripts; <script type=module>, fetch() and XHR of local JSON are all blocked; data must ship as .js (window.RK_DATA=...).

External SVG sprite is blocked under file:// ('file: URLs are treated as unique security origins'); inline sprites, , CSS background-image and (Chromium) mask-image work -> Python builder must inline only the icons actually used.
Lottie path: loading fails under file:// (XHR); only animationData from a .js wrapper works. dotLottie (ESM + WASM) cannot run offline.

Fonts in a fonts/ subfolder load under file:// in Chromium; Firefox fixed file:// font loading in 68.0.2/70 (bug 1565942), but fonts must sit in the document's directory or a subdirectory, never a parent directory. Offer a --embed-fonts base64 option as a fallback.

Top data-journalism stacks (Pudding svelte-starter, Reuters graphics-components) ship NO animation library: framework transitions/d3 + raw IntersectionObserver + sticky layout. Pudding's Scrolly is ~80 lines of IO.

Professional motion rules: 100-500ms UI (NN/g), chart entry 400-700ms with 30-60ms stagger and <=900ms total, data updates tween from old to new values (ECharts animationDurationUpdate + universalTransition), ease-out on entry and faster exits, staged transitions for complex changes (Heer & Robertson 2007). Avoid parallax, bounce/elastic, scroll-jacking, scroll-scrubbed key numbers, typewriter effects, looping motion.

Gap in kit/core/rk.motion.js: charts that mount on scroll will print or export to PDF blank. Add beforeprint/matchMedia('print') hooks that mount all charts with animation:false, call document.getAnimations().forEach(a=>a.finish()), then resize. For Playwright PDF export use emulateMedia({media:'print', reducedMotion:'reduce'}).

Other rk.motion additions: listen to prefers-reduced-motion changes; add a ?motion=off URL flag; add an RK.motion.swap() View Transitions wrapper for all filter re-renders; make count-up screen-reader safe (aria-label holds the final value); tween counts from the old value; skip animation when document.hidden.

GSAP's 2025 Webflow license dropped the old 'cannot charge end users' clause but is still non-OSI: amendable at any time, terminable at Webflow's discretion, and it bans use in no-code visual animation builders that compete with Webflow. Many web articles still quote the obsolete clause.

ESM-only libraries can be vendored as IIFE with esbuild at vendor time (measured): motion/mini animate + inView + stagger = 4.4 KB gz; anime.js subset = 17 KB gz (vs 40.6 KB full); number-flow = 5.2 KB gz. Extend tools/vendor.py with a 'build' entry type so the runtime never needs a bundler.

Fontsource (Google Fonts-derived) woff2 subsets strip most OpenType features (verified with fontTools). Inter keeps only tnum/pnum/frac (no zero/case/ss/cv) and has proportional default digits, so the kit's tabular-nums CSS still works. Upstream inter-ui 4.1.1 variable-latin subset (~100 KB) keeps every feature. IBM Plex, Source Serif 4, Source Sans 3 and Noto Sans SC have tabular digits by default.

OFL Reserved Font Names: IBM Plex reserves 'Plex' and Adobe Source fonts reserve 'Source', so don't self-subset them under the original name. Inter, Noto Sans SC (noto-cjk), JetBrains Mono and Roboto Mono have no RFN, so the builder can subset them freely. Fontsource LICENSE files sometimes list only 'Google Inc.' as copyright holder, so ship the upstream OFL text.

Recommended CJK strategy: use the builder to pyftsubset Noto Sans SC down to the report's own text (typically <200 KB), fall back to system CJK fonts for dynamic text, and optionally include the 101-chunk unicode-range set (4.5 MB) for full coverage.

Maintenance red flags found: Pico.css archived 2026-10-04 (no longer maintained), Tippy.js archived 2024-11-09, Shoelace archived (moved to Web Awesome), flatpickr has not released since 2022, AOS since 2018, and typed.js is now GPL-3.0.

Platform status (2026-10): same-document View Transitions are Baseline (Oct 2025, Firefox 144); CSS anchor positioning is Baseline (Jan 2026, Firefox 147); Popover API and @starting-style are Baseline 2024; scroll-driven animations are not Baseline (Firefox still behind a flag); appearance:base-select and interpolate-size are Chromium-only. Corporate locked-down browsers lag, so always feature-detect and fall back.
For finance-heavy filters, period presets (MTD/QTD/YTD/1Y/3Y/5Y) plus native <input type=month/date> beat calendar widgets. Calendars (Air Datepicker) are optional.

Icon pairing: Lucide (ISC, 24px/2px stroke) as the primary set plus Tabler Icons (MIT, same grid, 366 finance/chart glyphs), with lu-/tb- id prefixes. Avoid icon webfonts (Tabler 507 KB, Phosphor ~150 KB per weight) and Phosphor's CDN-injecting index.js.

angles.summary:
ECharts should stay the kit's only general chart engine. Nearly every Chinese dashboard template, low-code BI tool and Python wrapper is built on it (DataEase, GoView, iDataV, BigDataView, and pyecharts 2.1, which now targets ECharts 6). The kit already pins echarts 6.1.0, so a second engine (G2 or VChart, +300–600 KB gz each) adds little.

The most useful finding is the official @echarts-x/* custom series (Apache-2.0, 2026-01). Each is a self-registering classic script of 2–15 KB that works from file://:
- bar-range gives a proper football-field chart.
- line-range covers ranges, fans and bands.
- violin, contour, segmented-doughnut and stage cover distributions, progress and timelines.
- word-cloud and liquid-fill replace the old ecomfe plugins, which still only support ECharts 5.

ECharts 6 features worth using:
- Design-token themes and runtime chart.setTheme() for light/dark.
- The matrix coordinate system for small multiples.
- Broken axes (verified working on 6.1).
- Automatic label anti-overlap.
- The 6.1 tooltip XSS fix.

One gotcha: ECharts candlesticks default to red-up / green-down (the Chinese convention). The kit needs a locale setting for this.

Security: the AntV npm namespace (and echarts-for-react) was compromised on 2026-05-19 by the "Mini Shai-Hulud" worm, which published 600+ malicious versions, all higher than the real latest versions. I verified the bad versions now return 404. The kit should pin exact versions, keep vendoring via npm pack (no install scripts), and record an integrity hash for each vendored file.

Pivot tables with subtotals are the one area where a Chinese library adds something the kit lacks. AntV S2 (302 KB gz, global S2) and VisActor VTable (531 KB gz; includes PivotChart and Gantt) are both MIT. Either is worth considering as a lazily loaded module, with Tabulator kept for flat tables.

For the future local-LLM step, the libraries themselves are poor bets:
- VMind is unmaintained; its repo is now VisActor/skills.
- LIDA has been stale since 2024 and works by executing Python code.
- AVA v4 has become a server-side Node framework.
- AntV's MCP chart server and Sive send data to hosted services.

What carries over is a pattern that GPT-Vis, VSeed, the echarts-mcp README and Chinese practitioners on Juejin all agree on. The LLM only fills in a minimal, schema-checked spec (chart type, dataset, dimensions, measures). A fixed compiler owns all styling, and charts are rendered before the text streams out. Our data/spec layer should follow VSeed's dimensions/measures shape. AntV T8-style inline number tags are a good fit for commentary boxes.

Chinese "data big-screen" style is not suitable for IB reports. That includes dark navy backgrounds, neon glow, glassmorphism, SVG tech borders, 3D, flying lines, liquid gauges, word clouds and 1920×1080 scale-to-fit. Worth borrowing: a restrained KPI count-up, linked highlighting, top-to-bottom storyline layout, the annotation vocabulary, and token discipline. VChart's veODesignLightFinance palette (navy/tan/oxblood) and tw93/Kami (paper background, one ink-blue accent) are good style references.

Xiaohongshu could not be read: search needs a login and signed API calls, and it is not indexed by the available search engines. Zhihu returned 403 and CSDN bodies are behind a script check. Community signals therefore come from Juejin (search API plus about 12 articles), Sogou WeChat search and CSDN titles.
insights: Security: on 2026-05-19 the 'Mini Shai-Hulud' worm hijacked npm account 'atool' and published 600+ malicious versions across 317-324 @antv/* packages, plus echarts-for-react, size-sensor and timeago.js. The bad versions were numbered above the real latest (e.g. g2 5.5.8/5.6.8 vs real 5.4.8), so any ^ range would have pulled them in. I verified they now return 404. Kit rules: exact pins, npm pack only (no lifecycle scripts), and a stored dist.integrity sha512 plus per-file sha256 checked by tools/vendor.py --check.

Adopt the official @echarts-x/* custom series (Apache-2.0, 2026-01). Each dist/<name>.auto.min.js is a 2-15 KB classic script that self-registers after echarts.min.js and works from file://; use it as series {type:'custom', renderItem:'bar-range'}. bar-range gives a native football-field chart and line-range covers bands and fan charts. violin, contour, segmented-doughnut and stage are also available. word-cloud and liquid-fill replace the unmaintained ecomfe plugins (peer echarts ^5).

ECharts 6 has a token theme system (lib/visual/tokens.js: neutral00-99, accent05-95, semantic aliases such as axisSplitLine and primary/secondary text) and chart.setTheme() for runtime switching without re-init. Generate both the CSS custom properties and echarts.registerTheme('ib-light'/'ib-dark'/'ib-print') from one token JSON.

Gotcha: ECharts candlestick defaults are red up (#eb5454) and green down (#47b262), the Chinese convention (红涨绿跌). Western IB readers expect the reverse. Add a convention token ('western'|'cn') that drives candlestick, waterfall and delta colours.

ECharts 6 matrix coordinate system: any series or component (grid, pie, heatmap, geo) can be placed in a table-like cell layout. Use it for think-cell-style peer panels and small multiples before reaching for VTable PivotChart or G2 facets.

ECharts 6 breaking changes to remember: the default theme and legend position changed (theme/v5.js restores them); geo/graph center percent base changed (legacyViewCoordSysCenterBase); rich text now inherits label style (richInheritPlainLabel:false); axis label anti-overflow is on by default (grid.outerBoundsMode:'none' to disable). 6.1.0 fixes a tooltip XSS in the lines series.

Pivot tables with subtotals are the one capability gap a Chinese library fills: AntV S2 2.7.2 (global S2, 302 KB gz, finance-style cross-tabs) or VisActor VTable 1.26.8 (global VTable, 531 KB gz, plus PivotChart charts-in-cells, which also needs VChart at +617 KB). Load either lazily, only on pages that need it. Keep Tabulator for flat tables.

AI chart generation consensus (GPT-Vis DSL, VSeed, the echarts-mcp README, Juejin '零幻觉交付' post): the LLM fills in only a minimal intent spec (chartType + dataset + dimensions/measures); a deterministic compiler owns style; JSON is validated and repaired; charts are pre-rendered and revealed during pseudo-streaming. Design the kit's spec now in VSeed's shape: dimensions[{id,label}], measures[{id,label,format,unit,parentId}], encodings, annotations.

VMind is dead: its repo was renamed to VisActor/skills, whose README says the VMind SDK is no longer maintained (npm frozen at 2.0.10, 2025-08). LIDA has been stale since 2024-03 and executes generated Python. AVA v4 is a Node framework. AntV's mcp-server-chart and Sive send data to hosted services. For step 2, copy the patterns, not the libraries.

Skills packaging pattern to copy for step 2 (VisActor/skills, antvis/chart-visualization-skills): SKILL.md + local references + templates + scripts + eval cases; the host agent supplies the model through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Note that VisActor-generated HTML loads from unpkg, and the storytelling skill uses GSAP (not an OSI license).

AntV T8 inline-entity syntax ([12.3%](delta_value, assessment=positive)) is an excellent, LLM-friendly format for IB commentary boxes with data-bound, consistently formatted numbers (18 KB gz). Vendor it pinned or re-implement it in the text-block component.

Offline traps in Chinese libraries: AntV Infographic fetches icons from www.weavefox.cn and Alibaba PuHuiTi fonts from assets.antv.antgroup.com at runtime. L7's logo control and textures load from alipayobjects.com, and its basemaps need AMap/Baidu/Tianditu keys. pyecharts defaults to the assets.pyecharts.org CDN. VisActor skill HTML loads from unpkg. The VMind UMD expects Node globals.

Maps: ECharts has not shipped china.json or world maps since v5. Never fetch boundaries at runtime from geo.datav.aliyun.com. China-facing deliverables may need officially approved national boundaries (审图号 / 'problem map' rules), so make the boundary dataset swappable per client jurisdiction. Flag for legal review.

Big-screen (数据大屏) idioms to reject for IB: dark navy backgrounds, neon (#00f5d4/#00bbf9/#9b5de5/#f15bb5), glow and gradients, glassmorphism, DataV SVG tech borders, 3D (echarts-gl), flying lines, liquid gauges, word clouds, auto-scrolling tables, 1920x1080 scale-to-fit (autofit.js). Ideas to borrow: a single restrained KPI count-up, linked highlighting, top-to-bottom/left-to-right storyline layout, markLine/markArea/markPoint annotations, token discipline.

Palette references: VChart veODesignLightFinance (#294C60 navy, #E2B890 tan, #9D0800 oxblood, #324BCC royal, #9CADC8 slate, #AD7F45 bronze) is the most pitchbook-like Chinese preset. tw93/Kami (paper #f5f4ed, a single ink-blue #1B365D accent, 'no gradients, no drop shadows, no 3D') matches the print-first IB look. GPT-Vis 'academy' is Tableau-10.

Feishu dataviz guide rules worth encoding as lint checks: line charts at most 5 series; pie under 9 categories; funnel at most 12 steps; area at most 3 series unless stacked; dual Y axes only for different units; legend bottom-centre on desktop and hidden for a single series; space priority marks > legend > axes > gridlines; avoid rotated labels.

Chinese fonts: only Source Han Sans / Noto Sans SC (OFL) is safe to bundle; subset per report with fonttools because full CJK fonts are 8-16 MB. LXGW WenKai and Smiley Sans are OFL but stylistically wrong for IB. Alibaba PuHuiTi, HarmonyOS Sans and MiSans use custom licenses, and TsangerJinKai is personal-use only. Support 万/亿 compact formatting for zh-CN (Intl.NumberFormat notation:'compact').

Xiaohongshu is not crawlable. Search needs a login and signed x-s API calls, the server-rendered page holds only shell strings, and site:xiaohongshu.com returns nothing in the available search engine. Zhihu returns 403 and CSDN bodies sit behind a script check. Juejin works (its search API plus a proof-of-work page check that a browser solves automatically), as does Sogou WeChat search. Many 2025-26 CSDN posts are AI-generated SEO content and some Juejin posts are marketing with false claims, so treat them as popularity signals only.

angles.summary: I surveyed 28 curated collections: awesome lists, plugin databases, galleries, chart-taxonomy sites and dashboard templates. Each was verified from shallow git clones, with category counts taken from the raw READMEs, versions and licenses from npm/jsDelivr, and stars from shields.io. The best catalog seed is hal9ai/awesome-dataviz (formerly fasouto, then javierluraschi; CC BY 4.0, last commit 2026-10-13, 4.4k stars). It has about 420 entries in 24 sections, and its JS part (about 133 entries) has a Financial charts section and already lists the 2025-26 newcomers (Flint, Vela, ChartGPU, mapcn, the perspective-dev org). For the gallery taxonomy, use the FT Visual Vocabulary: 72 chart types in 9 relationship categories, in a machine-readable chartTypes.csv (MIT for the software; FT branding is excluded). Use data-to-viz as a second filter: 6 data-shape roots leading to about 39 charts, plus 12 caveats. Data Viz Catalogue (60 methods) and Datavizproject (166 types) are copyrighted, so use them only to check completeness. For reference code, the Apache ECharts examples are the strongest gallery: 377 2D plus 59 GL examples, Apache-2.0, with machine-readable category and 'since' tags. ECharts 6 adds features that suit finance work: axis breaks for intraday gaps and a matrix coordinate system for sparklines and mini-bars inside tables. Vega-Lite has 203 gallery examples (BSD-3) and Plotly has 12 gallery sections. The official Leaflet plugin DB has 578 plugins in 36 categories with frontmatter metadata. 568 are flagged compatible with v1 and none with v2, so pin Leaflet 1.9.4. Use chartjs/awesome as the Chart.js plugin matrix, but its version badges are out of date: chartjs-chart-financial 0.2.1 actually works with chart.js ^4 per npm. The catalogs also exposed traps. ApexCharts is under a dual Community/Commercial license from 5.1.0 (current 8.2.0), which rules it out for a bank, and Tabler's demos still use ApexCharts 7. MapLibre 6.x is ESM-only (the last UMD build is 5.24.0). WASM libraries (Perspective, Vizzu, Mosaic) fail under file://. The AntV cloud-rendering skill and MCP server send data off the machine. AdminLTE 4.10 is license-clean (Chart.js 4.5.1, jsvectormap, Tabulator; all MIT), while Tabler should be used only for CSS and icons. shadcn charts (70 Recharts 3.8 blocks) and Tremor Raw/Blocks are React-only design references. For Step 2, study Microsoft Flint (one MIT spec that compiles to Vega-Lite, ECharts, Chart.js, Plotly or Excel, with an MCP server) and AntV's SKILL.md packs, Infographic and GPT-Vis (MIT; UMD builds available). My concrete recommendation is a catalog.json keyed by FT category and data shape, linked to ECharts, Vega-Lite and Plotly example ids, which can also serve as the tool manifest the future LLM reads.
insights: Gallery navigation: use FT Visual Vocabulary's 9 categories as the primary axis and data-to-viz data shapes as the secondary filter. angles.summary:
Formula engine: keep the kit's own RK.expr (kit/core/rk.expr.js) and do not adopt a library.
- It has no eval or new Function and still works under a strict CSP. It was the fastest engine measured: 100k-row per-row eval in 14 ms, against 45–72 ms for math.js, expr-eval-fork and filtrex.
- It already has the bank-specific syntax: % literals, @params, backtick-quoted titles, aggregates, and n.m./n.a. handling.
- Add a function registry, plus an optional Excel financial-function pack from Formula.js 4.6.1 (MIT, UMD, CSP-safe; IRR, XNPV and PMT verified).
- Avoid expr-eval ≤2.0.2: CVE-2025-12735 is a remote-code-execution flaw rated 9.8.

Client query language: keep RK.query and treat its spec object as the single query format (intermediate representation) for charts, saved views and LLM output.
- Measured 17 ms at 10k rows, 45 ms at 100k and about 0.7 s at 1M rows for a 40-group group-by.

Optional SQL console: DuckDB-WASM.
- Pin 1.32.0 (wraps DuckDB 1.4.3). Gotcha: npm's 'latest' tag points to dev builds; 1.33.1-dev65.0 wraps DuckDB 1.5.6.
- It ran fully offline from a double-clicked file:// page using three tricks:
  - the ESM main module is shipped as a string and loaded with import() from a Blob URL, with its bare 'apache-arrow' import rewritten to the global Arrow 17 build;
  - the worker source is shipped as a string and started from a Blob URL;
  - the wasm is shipped as base64 inside a classic script and instantiated from a data: URL. A Blob URL fails because a worker started from file:// cannot fetch the page's Blob URLs.
- Cost: about 46 MB on disk and 2–4 s to start. Benefit: about 111 ms group-by and 50 ms median over 1M rows.
- Lock it down with enable_external_access=false plus lock_configuration=true, and use json_serialize_sql as a SELECT-only guard.
- sql.js is the light fallback (0.9 MB; pass wasmBinary on the first init call). It is slow beyond 100k rows.

Avoid AlaSQL for typed SQL: its double-backtick syntax runs arbitrary inline JavaScript (verified by the probe), and it needs eval. Arquero, AlaSQL and filtrex all fail under a strict CSP. The vendored ECharts 6.1 and Leaflet 1.9.4 pass, so a strict CSP is achievable for the whole kit.

Cross-filter: keep RK.store. It already has crossfilter semantics (each chart excludes its own filter). Use Mosaic as the architecture reference only; it ships only ESM source, needs DuckDB and has had breaking releases monthly. For scale, move to columnar storage with bitset filters, and switch to DuckDB above about 500k rows.

Local LLM: pages opened from file:// send Origin: null.
- Ollama's default allow-list includes file://*, which does not match null. Setting OLLAMA_ORIGINS=null makes Ollama panic at startup (from reading the gin-cors source; not tested against a live Ollama); only '*' or 'null*' work.
- vLLM now disables CORS by default. llama.cpp echoes any origin. LM Studio needs its CORS toggle.
- Chrome's Local Network Access prompt (Chrome 142+) behaviour for file:// pages is unspecified.
- Allowing null is equivalent to letting any website drive the local model API.
- Recommendation: a small Python companion that serves the report on 127.0.0.1 and proxies only the chat/models routes with a token.

The LLM should return JSON intents checked against a schema (query, metric, filter, data-only chart spec, read-only SQL), never code. They run locally, a strict CSP connect-src limits outbound requests to the LLM endpoint, and the model gets the schema and aggregates rather than raw rows.

Skills: use an Agent Skills SKILL.md for the LLM, plus an rk-skill.json manifest for declarative contributions, plus an optional classic-script skill.js. Code runs in a sandboxed srcdoc iframe (verified working on file://) over JSON-RPC via postMessage, modelled on MCP Apps.
insights: file:// facts measured in Chromium 141 headless: origin is 'null', isSecureContext=true, no SharedArrayBuffer. fetch/XHR of local files, new Worker(file) and import(file) are all blocked. Blob workers and import(blobURL) work. A blob worker cannot fetch the page's blob URLs but can fetch data: URLs (30 MB tested). IndexedDB, localStorage and the Cache API work; OPFS throws SecurityError. Sandboxed srcdoc iframes work and cannot read the parent.

The general recipe for any ESM + worker + wasm library on file:// is: ship the ESM source as a string in a classic script and load it with import() from a Blob URL, rewriting bare imports to UMD globals; ship the worker source as a string and start it from a Blob URL; ship the wasm as base64 in a classic script and pass it as a data:application/wasm URL. Verified with DuckDB-WASM 1.32.0.

Raw on-disk size, not gzip size, is the load cost on file://, because browsers do not decompress local files. Example: the DuckDB power-pack is about 46 MB as base64 and needs 2-4 s to instantiate, so it must be lazy-loaded behind a builder flag.

A strict CSP without unsafe-eval breaks Arquero, AlaSQL and filtrex. It does not break RK.expr, sql.js asm, math.js, expr-eval-fork, jsep, JSONata, Formula.js, ECharts 6.1.0 or Leaflet 1.9.4. Emit a strict meta CSP from the builder, with connect-src limited to the LLM endpoint, to make data exfiltration by a prompt-injected LLM impossible (verified that external fetch is blocked). Add a CSP smoke test for every vendored library.

The kit's existing RK.expr beat every library on safety, speed (14 ms per 100k rows) and domain syntax. Extend it with a function registry, IB window functions (lag, pct_change, cagr, rank) and Formula.js financial functions, rather than replacing it.

Use the RK.query spec object (from, select[{expr, as, format}], by, where, sort, limit) as the single query format for charts, saved views, LLM intents and engines. RK.query executes it by default; it compiles to DuckDB SQL when the power-pack is on.

Before reaching for DuckDB, columnar internal storage (typed arrays, dictionary-encoded strings, per-filter bitsets) would bring RK.query from about 0.7 s to about 0.15-0.25 s at 1M rows. Also consider a columnar or Arrow-IPC-base64 option in the data contract.

DuckDB-WASM gotchas: the npm 'latest' tag is a dev build; 1.32.0 requires apache-arrow 17; BIGINT results come back as BigInt and break JSON.stringify; DECIMAL comes back as strings; the COI bundle is unusable on file://. To harden it: SET enable_external_access=false; SET lock_configuration=true; and use json_serialize_sql to reject anything that is not a SELECT.
AlaSQL's double-backtick syntax is an arbitrary-JavaScript execution surface (verified), so never feed it untrusted, LLM-generated or shared SQL.

Local LLM CORS: pages opened from file:// send Origin: null, plus a preflight because of the JSON content type.
- Ollama: its default file://* entry does not match null. OLLAMA_ORIGINS=null panics in gin-cors Validate; use '*' or 'null*'. This is from reading the source, not a live test.
- vLLM: --allowed-origins now defaults to [].
- llama.cpp: echoes any origin, with credentials.
- LM Studio: needs its 'Enable CORS' toggle.
- Allowing null effectively allows any website, via sandboxed iframes.

Chrome Local Network Access (142+; split in 145 into local-network and loopback-network permissions) gates requests to loopback. Its behaviour for file:// pages is 'weakly specified', so test it on the bank's browser or push the LocalNetworkAccessAllowedForUrls policy. A Python companion serving the report on 127.0.0.1 and proxying only the chat/models routes avoids CORS, LNA and admin-endpoint exposure, and unlocks fetch, ES modules and workers.

LLM contract: the model returns JSON intents constrained by a schema (query, metric, filter, data-only rk-chart spec, read-only SQL, answer) through response_format or tools on any OpenAI-compatible server. The page validates them locally (RK.expr.check / RK.query.parse / the SQL guard), executes them, shows the editable formula, and feeds errors back to the model for at most 2 retries.
- Never let the model write ECharts options or HTML formatters, and never put LLM text into innerHTML.
- Send the schema, data dictionary and aggregates, not raw rows, and keep an audit log in IndexedDB.

Text-to-chart references: GPT-Vis has an LLM-friendly streaming DSL and NL4DV has structured JSON intents; LIDA generates and executes code, which is unsafe. Local text-to-SQL candidates for IT: Arctic-Text2SQL-R1 (7B-32B), Qwen3-Coder, DuckDB-NSQL (on Ollama). For the kit's own query dialect, few-shot examples in the system prompt matter more than a SQL-specialised model.

Skills: follow the open Agent Skills format for the LLM-facing part. SKILL.md frontmatter has name (64 chars max, lowercase and hyphens, must match the folder) and description (1024 chars max), with optional license, compatibility, metadata and allowed-tools. Loading is progressive: name and description, then the body (under 500 lines), then references.
- Add an rk-skill.json manifest for runtime contributions (functions, metrics, queries, charts, prompts, tools, permissions) and an optional classic-script skill.js wrapper for file://.
- Imported (untrusted) skills get declarative contributions only; their code runs in a sandboxed srcdoc iframe with an inner CSP and no network, over JSON-RPC via postMessage modelled on MCP Apps.

In-browser LLMs: WebGPU is available on file://, but WebLLM and transformers.js weights must be fetched over http(s), so they suit companion or intranet mode only. wllama can load a user-picked GGUF on file:// but runs single-threaded. Chrome's Prompt API status for web pages in 2026 is contested and it is Chrome-only, so offer it only as an optional extra.

angles.summary: I measured the file:// constraints in Chromium 156 and Firefox 157 instead of relying on folklore. Both block fetch, XHR, ES modules (static and dynamic import()), file-based Workers, Service Workers, iframe DOM access, cssRules on linked stylesheets, and canvas export after drawing a local . Classic
insights: file:// behaviour measured in Chromium 156 and stock Firefox 157. BLOCKED: fetch/XHR of local JSON,

Test-harness trap: Playwright's bundled Firefox sets security.fileuri.strict_origin_policy=false in playwright.cfg, so fetch, modules and workers appear to work on file://. CI must pass firefox_user_prefs={'security.fileuri.strict_origin_policy': True}.

Data transport: write data/<id>.json (canonical, for HTTP/API) and data/<id>.js = RK.data.register(id, JSON.parse("...")) from the same serialized string. Lazy-load per page via script injection; never assign globals.

Benchmark (40k rows x 15 fields, file://, median of 5). Chromium: records literal 372 ms vs JSON.parse 133 ms; columns literal 110 ms vs JSON.parse 79 ms. Firefox: 411/220/177/160 ms. Sizes: records 9.3 MB vs columns 5.8 MB; gzipped 3.08 vs 2.28 MB. Use JSON.parse above 10 kB (V8 guidance) and offer orient:'columns'.

Python serialization gotchas: json.dumps(NaN) emits 'NaN', which is invalid JSON and makes JSON.parse throw, so map NaN/Inf to null + flag and dump with allow_nan=False. pandas 3 to_json without date_format warns that epoch is deprecated. orient='table' datetimes have no Z, so new Date() parses date-only strings as UTC but datetime strings as local time, which can shift days. Make 'date' values YYYY-MM-DD strings parsed without timezone conversion.

Contract = Frictionless Table Schema v2 names (fields, type, format, constraints, categories, labelled missingValues, primaryKey) plus finance extensions: unit {currency, scale, kind}, Excel-style format, role (key/label/dimension/measure/time/geo.*), default aggregate (multiples default to median, never sum), polarity, cell flags[] linked to footnotes, meta.source[]/footnotes[]/asOf/lineage, version + sha256 hash, orient records|columns|rows.

Spec shape: components{} map (elements) separate from pages[].items[] grid placement that references them (Grafana schema v2). Bindings use Vega-Lite / Graphic Walker channel names (x, y, color, size, shape, opacity, theta, radius, latitude, longitude, geoId, detail, label, tooltip) and compile to ECharts dataset/encode/visualMap. Params use $name; selections use Mosaic resolution (crossfilter: a component's own clause never filters itself).

Versioning: $schema + specVersion with migration chains in both JS and Python (Vega-Lite, Grafana schemaVersion, Graphic Walker IChart.$schema + migrate()). Datasets carry contract tag, version and hash; manifest carries client revision, changelog, generator/kit versions and file checksums. Each delivered folder freezes its own kit + vendor copies (Plotly include_plotlyjs='directory' precedent) so it renders identically years later.

Print: 1280x720 CSS px = 13.333in x 7.5in = PowerPoint 16:9. With @page{size:13.333in 7.5in; margin:0} Chromium produced exact 960x540 pt pages, so fixed-geometry slides need no print-time chart resize, and Ctrl+P works without beforeprint timing hacks.

PDF evidence: ECharts canvas charts become raster images (560x360 at DPR1 in headless) with no selectable text; the SVG renderer stays vector with extractable labels. Default to SVG for report charts; use canvas plus devicePixelRatio 2-3 only for dense series.

beforeprint and matchMedia('print') change events fire during headless page.pdf(), but the builder should still call RK.print.prepare() explicitly (animation:false, resize, invalidateSize) and await document.fonts.ready.

Browser support (MDN BCD 8.1.5): @page size in Chrome 15, Firefox 95, Safari 18.2; page margin boxes only in Chrome/Edge 131+ (not Firefox or Safari). Render footers, page numbers and confidentiality lines in the DOM with CSS counters and treat margin boxes as an enhancement. print-color-adjust unprefixed needs Chrome 136+, so also emit -webkit-print-color-adjust.
On-screen scaling of fixed slides: transform: scale(k) kept ECharts 6.1 hover and Leaflet 1.9.4 clicks correct in both browsers. CSS zoom:0.6 made ECharts report the wrong bar in both, so avoid zoom.
Paged.js 0.4.3 (last stable 2023) fails on file:// when print CSS is a <link> (it XHRs the stylesheet) but runs with inline <style>; do not depend on it. Vivliostyle is AGPL; avoid.

Avoid as runtime deps on file://: Perspective (moved to @perspective-dev 5.6.0; ESM + import.meta.url + WASM fetch), DuckDB-WASM (npm latest is a dev build; needs workers + WASM), Graphic Walker (UMD needs React 19 globals; React 19.3.0 ships no UMD), Observable Framework/Notebook Kit and Evidence output (ESM + fetch; Framework's deploy deprecated, Evidence docs now centre on `evidence serve`), Datapane (unmaintained since 0.17.0, 2023-09).

Single-file mode (--single-file) for email or portal upload: inline CSS/JS, datasets as <script type='application/json' id='rk-data-<id>'>, fonts and images as base64; escape '<' as <. Precedents: Quarto embed-resources, Plotly include_plotlyjs=True, Altair inline=True, Bokeh INLINE. HTML attachments are often blocked by gateways (HTML smuggling), so the default delivery is a zipped folder plus PDF via data room.

Chrome shares one localStorage bucket across all file:// pages, so namespace keys rk:<report.id>:<revision>: and keep only UI state there. HTML-escape all data text by default (Great Tables 1.0 made escaping its default) and allow a safe markdown subset.

Great Tables 1.0 (2026-09-25) is the table-anatomy reference for our table spec: title/subtitle, spanners, stub + row groups with indentation, summary_rows, cell-targeted footnotes, source notes, sub_missing, fmt_* incl. number_si/engineering/fraction, data_color, nanoplots, define_units.

Builder pipeline borrowed from Observable Framework: loaders/<id>.json.py writes to stdout (logs to stderr), non-zero exit fails the build, outputs are cached by loader + input hash, and only datasets referenced by the spec are built. Analysts write df.to_json(orient='table', date_format='iso') plus a <id>.meta.yaml sidecar for titles, units, formats, sources and footnotes.

Step-2 readiness: JSON Schema (from pydantic) for spec and contract lets a local LLM propose JSON Patches or formulas that are validated before apply. Field description/unit/role/aggregate double as a semantic layer (Rill metrics-view idea). A local LLM endpoint called from file:// is a cross-origin request from origin null, so the server must allow CORS (*/null).

libraries.name: Mosaic (vgplot/mosaic-core)

libraries.name: Panel / Bokeh

libraries.name: Quarto dashboards

libraries.name: Rill

libraries.name: Datapane
libraries.capabilities: Python -> standalone HTML reports
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes (inlined HTML)

libraries.name: Metabase
libraries.capabilities: BI server; embedding
libraries.offline_classic_script: No

libraries.reason: Tiny official extension that renders the football field directly, so no hand-rolled custom renderItem is needed.

libraries.name: Apache ECharts
libraries.capabilities:
Native coverage of nearly every IB chart type in one script:
- bar, line, scatter, pie, sankey
- chord (new in v6), treemap with drill-down, sunburst
- boxplot, candlestick, heatmap, calendar, parallel
- radar, funnel, gauge, graph (force/circular)
- geo/map choropleth with scatter, lines and flows
- themeRiver, pictorialBar, tree

Also new in v6: matrix coordinate layout, beeswarm/jitter and axis breaks.

Waterfall, Marimekko and football field are custom-series recipes (verified). SVG and canvas renderers. Node SSR via renderToSVGString.
libraries.interactions_animation:
Interaction:
- dataZoom (inside and slider)
- brush (rect, polygon, lineX/Y) with events
- echarts.connect for linked tooltips and zoom
- legend filtering
- setOption diff updates, with replaceMerge for data swaps
- universalTransition morphs and label valueAnimation
- runtime setTheme (v6)
- large-data sampling (LTTB) and progressive rendering

Animation is among the best of the OSS engines.
libraries.multi_dim_encoding:
visualMap maps any data dimension to colour, colorAlpha, lightness, saturation, symbolSize, symbol or opacity.
- Several visualMaps can target different dimensions (6.1 seriesTargets).
- symbolSize and itemStyle callbacks give per-point encodings.
- decal patterns act as an extra categorical channel.
- A geo instance combines proportional symbols, choropleth and flow lines.
libraries.offline_classic_script:
Yes. Verified on file:// in Chromium 141.
- dist/echarts.min.js is the full UMD build; echarts.common.min.js and echarts.simple.min.js are lighter UMD builds.
- theme/*.js and i18n/lang*.js are UMD.
- Maps must be registered from a JS global; fetching them fails on file://.
libraries.size: 1095 KB min / 359 KB gz (full); 233 KB gz common; 164 KB gz simple
libraries.reason:
It is the only permissive, ASF-governed engine with near-complete IB coverage in one classic script.
- Dual SVG/canvas rendering gives vector print and big-data performance; both were verified.
- It has the deepest theming of the OSS engines, plus runtime setTheme.
- Interaction is mature.
- Node SSR fallback works.
- pyecharts 2.1 targets v6.

The gaps (waterfall, Mekko, football field, CAGR annotations) are proven 20–40-line custom series.

Broad scientific and financial coverage:

- sankey, treemap, sunburst, icicle

- 3D surface, geo choropleth, quiver (new in v4)

No chord, calendar or force graph. Partial bundles are available (finance 436 KB gz).
libraries.interactions_animation: Excellent built-in interaction: drag-zoom, pan, rangeslider, box/lasso select events, hover modes and a modebar with SVG/PNG export. Animation is limited (Plotly.animate).
libraries.multi_dim_encoding: marker.size, color, symbol and opacity arrays; colorscales; facets via subplots.

libraries.size: 1441 KB gz full; 422 KB gz finance; 388 KB gz basic
libraries.reason:
Optional, narrow complement for plotly.py parity or scientific charts (parcats, splom, 3D).

- The default look needs heavy templating to match a pitchbook.

libraries.name: Vega-Lite + Vega + vega-embed
libraries.capabilities:
Declarative grammar-of-graphics.
- Marks: bar, line, area, point, rect/heatmap, boxplot, arc, geoshape, text, rule, tick.

libraries.multi_dim_encoding: x, y, color, size, shape, opacity, strokeDash, row/column facet; fully declarative.
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes. build/vega.min.js, build/vega-lite.min.js and build/vega-embed.min.js are still UMD, even though Vega 6 is 'ESM-only' at package level. Verified on file://.
libraries.reason:
Use as a lazy-loaded complement for an explore/ask console.
- Native cross-filtering.
- The most LLM-friendly, schema-validatable chart grammar.
- Altair interop for Python analysts.

Not suitable as the pitchbook engine: no animation, missing IB types, alphabetical default sort and an academic look.
